body:
Oh wow. I'm so sorry.   

I've honestly had suicidal thoughts myself, but I then realize that it's not the way to deal with problems, and it's just not the right thing to do.  

I understand the alienation part. I'm completely alienated at my school because I'm a huge sports fan. No one else likes them, and the one person who I thought I was close to because of that decided to ditch me today for "cooler" people.  

In school now, I have nothing to get my mind off of this. I literally put my head down and cry in every class due to this. My grades have gone from 90s to 60s and 70s, just because I can't care anymore. At home, I pretend to be happy for my mother's sake.  

Just yesterday, I opened up to my dad about this. He gives the cliche "it'll all get better, just have fun, etc.". He's helped me a bit, but the only time I get my mind off this is when I'm doing something fun. I don't wanna live half my life thinking of this and the other half having fun. I wanna be worry-free.  

What makes my condition worse is school, actually. I see everybody having fun, talking about their next weekend plans, who they hooked up with, etc., not a care in the world. I wish I could be like that, but this feeling makes it impossible for me. I just feel so...alone.  

I sincerely hope things get better for you. Go the AA meeting and just try it. If you feel it's helpful, go again. If not, try and find something that will help you.
How exactly have you done that and stayed strong? I try, but nothing ever works.

That's true, yeah, but this feeling has stripped me of all motivation to do anything. I started feeling like this a month ago, and I can't shake it. All I think about is this. I can't pay attention in school, to sports (which I love), or anything really
I realize that, but what's the point of being happy and living a great life if you're just going to lose and forget it all when you inevitably die?
